decisions.reason: The compatible splitting maps retain (M_0)_a; omitting it gives a false isomorphism even for A=B=M=Z with the zero algebra generator. Restored that summand, distinct denominators for M_0 and the N early quotients (including N=0), the product over nonzero filtration primes, and inherited AC accounting. The stabilized kernels give only finitely many quotient types; localization and compatible splittings then prove freeness without a finite-rank claim. Stacks 051R confirms the theorem via a different prime-filtration/dimension proof; no claim of independent review of this repair.

The repository definition of Noetherian allows noncommutative rings, whereas associated-prime localization and the cited existence theorem require commutativity. Added that missing hypothesis. For nonzero a, an annihilator witness b in Ra forces a to survive at Ann(b); the localized witness is killed by the maximal ideal and gives depth zero. AC supplies the dependent-choice hypothesis of the existence theorem.

The owning page contains flat base-change and composition lemmas but no faithfully-flat stability proofs. Removed the unsupported page promise; retained exactly flat plus surjective and the quasi-compact single-morphism fpqc convention. Target locality follows pointwise, identities and open covers induce identity local rings, and the empty cases hold. The sole direct consumer thm-faithfully-flat-descent-vanishing uses only flatness, surjectivity and fpqc in F1 and 1.1–1.3, so this deletion leaves those uses sound.

The actual Statement explicitly promises exactness in every positive degree, and the displayed complex has no terminal arrow to zero. The title is conventional shorthand for this precise claim, not an additional assertion H_0=0. Multiplication by x satisfies the claim and is not a counterexample. Unit splitting preserves the minor ideals; the top minimal term forces depth at least its degree; nonmaximal localizations lower dimension; highest finite-length homology is excluded by the depth lemma. The contract also consistently specifies positive exactness. No cosmetic edit made.

F1 inferred containment of all proper ideals from uniqueness of a maximal ideal without supplying maximal-ideal existence above each ideal. That implication is not licensed in ZF by def-local-ring. Added AC and the proved proper-ideal containment theorem, then the cyclic submodule A/Ann(x) tensors to the nonzero B/Ann(x)B and flatness gives nonzero detection. This repairs the exactness-reflection proof. Entin states the MIT/AC equivalence; the repair itself uses the repository Zorn proof, not a claimed independent verification of that equivalence.

The fibre after an arbitrary field extension is not called a geometric fibre under def-geometric-fibre, which fixes an algebraic closure. Corrected the name while retaining every field extension and point in the defining quantifier. Local dimension remains infimum over neighbourhoods, with the component formula restricted to finite-type field charts; no numerical invariant or hypothesis changed. All direct consumers use that unchanged dimension convention, including dimension-zero etaleness and standard-chart parameter counts.

The rejection confuses an item with its owning page. library/scheme-theory/flat-smooth-and-etale-morphisms.md explicitly includes thm-smooth-locus-open. Its steps 1.1–3.1 obtain an invertible-minor principal neighbourhood at each smooth point and hence openness; step 4.1 proves smoothness of the restriction. The definition correctly defines a subset by the three germ conditions and makes no assumption of openness. The promise is fulfilled by that separate theorem; no edit is needed.

F6 attributed localization flatness to a corollary that only supplies free-module flatness. Removed that unused assertion: steps 1.3 and 2.2 use free modules over the localized base, with their bases preserved under further scalar extension. Finite source covers exist by quasi-compactness, products of nonzero denominators stay nonzero in each domain, and the restricted charts cover all of the preimage. Empty source covers use product one. Statement and generic-flatness claim are unchanged.

F11 must retain the nonzero-ring convention of the dimension definition. Added it; all rings used in the dimension calculation are nonzero domains or localizations at the displayed prime. Also corrected the harmless description of h-t: its leading coefficient in t is -1, a unit, rather than 1. The map k[t] into k[x,y] is injective by y-degree, hence torsion-free and flat over the PID. Irreducibility follows because x^2(x+1) is not a polynomial square; the prime chain gives local dimension one while the quadratic relation leaves two cotangent generators.

Degree greater than one is not an obstruction: two identity components form an etale degree-two finite flat cover. Replaced the misleading degree explanation by the nonreduced geometric fibres of Frobenius. Also aligned the explicit all-field-extensions condition with the smoothness definition: the base-changed fibre has regular local rings, rather than calling every extension a geometric fibre. The primary definition smooth of relative dimension zero, all germ restrictions, and empty cases are unchanged.

B to B tensor kappa(p) is generally not surjective. Each normalization generator instead has form y_i/a_i with a_i outside p; multiplying by the nonzero scalar a_i preserves algebraic independence and the polynomial subalgebra over kappa(p). These scaled generators lift and give the required quasi-finite polynomial map. Also cleared the second principal-open denominator back to the original B. The finite-algebra factorization bounds every fibre local ring by n, hence all prime chains and the neighbourhood dimension by n. Statement unchanged; no new prerequisite needed.

F6 incorrectly applied the component formula to arbitrary locally Noetherian schemes; restrict it to finite-type field neighbourhoods, which include all chart fibres used in 5.1. Also repaired the stronger false global rank assertion: smoothness at one point gives local freeness near that point, not on all X. Restricted Statement and 7.1 to the smooth locus, preserving the global conclusion for smooth f. Distinguished the invertible Jacobian block from its determinant in 2.1/4.1 and corrected B_0 localization in 3.1. Block elimination gives cokernel rank m-c, equal to component dimension after every field extension.

F6 used the height of the quotient prime Q where the supplier uses the polynomial-ring prime Q prime. For k[t]/(t), the ambient height one minus one is zero, whereas quotient height zero minus one is false. Corrected the prime and its ambient ring. The proof uses the valid component dimension m-r, not the erroneous local-ring formula: standard-smooth charts give both directions and the common fibre dimension. Also made AC accounting include F6 and distinguish finite selections. Statement unchanged.

F1 omitted AC from arbitrary-basis projectivity, although no projectivity is used. Retained precisely the supplier choice-free free-module flatness clause, and specified the choice-free direction from affine algebra flatness to stalkwise flatness. Monomial coefficients give the free module, the empty equation list is finitely presented, and the AC-qualified Jacobian criterion yields smooth relative dimension n. The flatness proof remains choice-free as contracted, including n=0 and the empty spectrum.

The fibre isomorphism identifies the points over the chosen y with a subset of the points over x, not necessarily all of them. Replaced the asserted correspondence by the needed inclusion: every tested point maps over x and therefore has the same dimension reldim_f(x). Smoothness after base change is supplied pointwise by the cited chart argument. For composition the two dimensions add, so zero plus zero remains zero. All global, pointwise and empty cases follow; the Statement is unchanged.

Clause 2 lacked the smoothness hypothesis required by its appeal to clause 1; the dual-number scheme over a field disproves the unconditional version. Restored if f is smooth and stated it at proof 2.1. Both global clauses now follow by the two successive base changes, and the pointwise clause uses the explicit pointwise standard-chart argument of the stability theorem. Corrected the all-field-extension fibre terminology without changing its quantifier. No direct dependency/reference item consumers were found; the owning page only lists the lemma.

The title asserted finite presentation rather than local finite presentation. An infinite disjoint union of identity points is etale but is not quasi-compact, so the title needed correction. The Statement and proof already have the right local hypothesis: smoothness gives local lifts and vanishing differentials gives uniqueness, since the difference of two lifts into a square-zero ideal is a derivation. Conversely formal smoothness plus local finite presentation gives smoothness, and formal unramifiedness gives zero differentials. Only the title changed.

F3 extended germ invariance to arbitrary subschemes, which is false for the closed origin in the affine line. Restored the supplier open-subscheme hypothesis. The proof uses it only for the open etale locus after openness is proved: an etale point has a standard smooth chart with m-r=0, and its unit square Jacobian remains invertible throughout the principal open. Thus every point of that open is etale and restriction to the resulting open locus is licensed. Statement unchanged.

The converse and infinite-union proofs invoked the AC-qualified etale criterion despite their choice-free claim. Preserved the stronger promised result by checking each open identity component directly: it is flat and finitely presented and every field-extended fibre is a regular zero-dimensional field. Finite products are module-finite; infinitely many nonempty open components have no finite subcover. The forward classification retains AC through F2/F3 and Artinian theory: stalks are finite separable fields, hence k, affine charts split, and quasi-compactness leaves finitely many points. Corrected step locators and explicitly separated the zero affine chart before dimension zero is invoked.
